newsitem.title: USA: Alliance sees Q2 charge, structure change.
newsitem.headline: Alliance sees Q2 charge, structure change.

text.p: Alliance Capital Management LP said Tuesday it expects to record a non-recurring, non-cash charge of $121 million, or $1.40 per unit, in the third quarter to reduce the recorded value of goodwill and contracts associated with its acquisition of Cursitor Holdings LP and Cursitor Holdings Ltd.

The company announced the charge in a statement in which it also said it has plans for a new ownership structure letting unitholders exchange their units for publicly traded common stock in a new corporation, Alliance Capital Management Corp II (ACMC II).
The company said it would not pursue the plan if changes in federal tax law make it preferable to retain the current ownership form.

Alliance said if the plan goes into effect, its distribution policy would remain unchanged, and ACMC II would pay substantially all of its pro rata distributions, less income taxes, as dividends to its common stockholders.
It said it would apply to list the Class A common stock on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company said it expects to report second quarter operating income, excluding the writedown of intangibles, of $0.66, and a second quarter net loss including the writedown of $0.74 per unit.

In line with these estimates, Alliance said it expects to declare a second quarter distribution of $0.64 per unit, compared to $0.55 and $0.60 per unit for the quarters ended June 30, 1996, and March 31, 1997, respectively.
It said full year 1997 distributions should be in the range of $2.60 to $2.65 per unit, versus $2.19 for 1996.

Operating income and distributions per unit for full year 1997 will be in the range of $2.68 to $2.73. The full year 1997 net income, including the writedown of intangibles and costs associated with the proposed restructuring, is estimated in the range of $1.17 to $1.22 per unit, the company said.

It said the non-recurring charge reflects its current view that Cursitor's continuing decline in assets under management and its reduced profitability no longer support the carrying value of its investment. It said Cursitor's assets under management have fallen from $10.1 billion at the date of acquisition to $5.3 billion as of May 31, 1997.
